title: unstructured-feedback-sparklines-and-microfeature-brief-2027-11-09
content:
Purpose / quick note:
This is a scratchpad-style synth of ~25 raw customer messages (support tickets, account calls, and NPS comments) for the week of 2027-10-25. Goal: extract high-probability microfeatures we can prototype in a day or two and map them to likely impact + quick implementation notes. Not a formal product proposal — treat as field notes for PM/Eng pairing.

Topline themes (high-level):
- Observability asks re: per-token cost spikes and KV-cache miss patterns (appears in 6 accounts across mid-market and enterprise).
- Predictable throttling behavior during scheduled bursts (accounts want clearer preemptive signals).
- Small ergonomics asks in the Console: exportable prompt/response pairs, per-route cost filters, and a quick way to mark/label model rollouts.
- Private deployment onboarding friction: env var/TLS handshake stories — mostly single-threaded docs gaps.
- One-off safety/response-quality regression examples tied to a model upgrade; customers asking for a safe rollback button (canary->fallback UI).

Signal sparklines (handy visual shorthand, ascii):
- Observability requests: |||||||||||||||||||| (6 strong signals)
- Console export/labels: ||||||||| (3-4 signals)
- Throttling transparency: |||||||| (4 signals)
- Private onboarding TLS docs: ||||| (2-3 signals)
- Safe rollback UI: |||| (2 signals but high severity)

Representative customer quotes (paraphrased):
- "We're getting charged weirdly on burst days — we need to see token spikes tied to model variants and cache misses." — fintech POC
- "Can we just download all prompts for a route for our compliance team? Right now we copy-paste which is painful." — health startup
- "We had a model upgrade and some generative answers started hallucinating. Need an easier way to put the old one back instantly." — enterprise search vendor

Microfeature candidates (sketches + why):
1) Route-level quick-export (CSV) for prompt/response + metadata
   - What: export last N requests per route with model, latency, token counts, and labels.
   - Why: compliance + root-cause for customer debug; immediate UX win for CS and customers.
   - Impact: high for accounts with compliance teams; medium engineering effort (backend filter + small CSV endpoint + Console button).
   - Quick implementation notes: reuse existing request-store index; add a short-lived presigned export job; console button -> polling UX.
   - Risks/Questions: data retention policy edge cases (GDPR), need filter by token redaction.

2) KV-cache miss telemetry toggle + simple visualization
   - What: expose per-request KV-cache hit/miss flag and a per-route miss rate chart in last-24h.
   - Why: customers keep blaming model behavior that is actually cache miss driven; this helps triage and shows cost drivers.
   - Impact: medium-high for customers using longer contexts.
   - Quick impl: small runtime hook to forward hit/miss booleans into metrics pipeline (inflight) + dashboard tile.
   - Notes: should sample initially to reduce ingestion cost; enable per-customer opt-in.

3) Canary rollback button (safe revert to pinned version)
   - What: Console action to quickly revert served model to last pinned stable version with explanatory logs.
   - Why: reduces mean-time-to-recover for response-quality regressions after upgrades.
   - Impact: high for enterprise customers; low-medium engineering complexity (requires tying rollout metadata to runtime and ensuring idempotent revert).
   - Safety: add confirmation flow and audit log; tie to Dedicated/Private only initially.

4) Pre-burst throttling notification API (webhook)
   - What: a webhook that notifies customers when their request rates approximate configured autoscale/burst thresholds.
   - Why: customers want to schedule behavior changes; reduces surprise throttles.
   - Impact: medium; helps large customers manage traffic.
   - Impl: use existing autoscaler hook points; add per-account webhook config.

5) Private-deploy quick TLS checklist + script bundle
   - What: small companion repo with checklist, script snippets for cert handling (example openssl commands), and common env var templates.
   - Why: reduces onboarding confusion and SRE time for private installs.
   - Impact: low-medium; very low dev time (docs + tiny repo).

Prioritization matrix (quick take):
- X axis = engineering effort (small -> large); Y axis = customer impact (low -> high)
- Quick-export: effort small-medium, impact high (priority 1)
- KV-cache telemetry: effort small, impact medium-high (priority 2)
- Canary rollback: effort medium, impact high (priority 1/2 for Dedicated/Private customers)
- Pre-burst webhook: effort small-medium, impact medium (priority 3)
- TLS checklist repo: effort trivial, impact small (priority 4; do as docs sprint)

Open questions / follow-ups (for CS -> PM):
- Data retention and PII redaction rules for exportable prompts. Legal review needed: tag to Legal. (linked artifact: JIRA CSREQ-1872)
- Sampling budget for KV-cache telemetry: what is acceptable ingestion cost? Ops/Infra input needed.
- Should rollback be allowed for hosted customers or gated to Dedicated/Private only? Risk profile differs.
- Can we ship a minimal rollback (routing flag flip) without a full audit UI and still meet compliance expectations?

Quick experiment proposals (week-of sprintable):
- Build a prototype export endpoint scoped to "last 100 requests for route" with automatic redaction of tokens flagged as sensitive. Use a temporary UI button visible only to internal CS. Run with 3 pilot customers for 2 weeks.
- Add a sampled KV-cache hit/miss boolean as a debug header to responses for 10% of requests for 7 days for 3 customers under support sandbox. Collect cost delta.

Operational notes / handoff
- Owner suggestion: PM: Marco Silva; Eng lead: Liam Chen; CS contact: Aisha Patel.
- Add Legal/Privacy review ticket for export redaction rules.
- Tagging: add support playbook for rollback flow if we expose the button.

Misc notes / rough quotes from tickets (raw):
- "Billing spike last Wed, not sure if it's model change or our test harness" (acct: fastloan-prod)
- "Need download for auditors next month — we can't do manual copy/paste" (acct: meddatasci)
- "After the upgrade on 10/19 some suggestions became wildly off; we rolled back and it's better but it took too long" (acct: corpsearch)

Immediate next steps (short):
- Monday 11/08: Quick sync w/Marco and Liam to sanity-check effort estimates (30m).
- Tuesday 11/09: Create JIRA spike for export prototype + Legal consult.
- Pilot plan draft by 11/15.

Notes to self (Aisha):
- Keep this doc intentionally rough; share with small triage group not the full CS channel.
- Keep snippets of raw quotes in ticket CSREQ-1872 for legal evidence.

End of scratchpad.
